title: How the dance boats worked and what they paid
summary: He explains the boats ran a quarter-a-dance cruise from downtown to Jackson Park, and the band played hard to draw people on, earning $16-17 a night.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: They had two boats, they had two boats out there, you know. Oh, yeah. They had two boats. They hadn't seen the North Shore, I was on the North Shore. There was boats just go up to the lake and dance, they play a quarter, like a, like a Jitney dance, like a Texan dance. You play a quarter and dance from downtown to Jackson Park out there. And she said, come back, and he play a quarter, get on the boat. We play like hell when they're leaving, and play like hell when we're coming back. When we're leaving, people just cruising and going off. Didn't play too much, I had to get out on the water. You get to play a ballyhoo lot, you get them on there. Yeah.
Yeah. You play like hell to get them on there. Yeah. You wind up, but well, $16, $17 a night was good money then days. Oh, yeah. They give us $1, that's where you cost that.
And so if it rains, you get the coffee. One dollar, but we make $16, $17 a night. That's how tough it was.
